title: Machine learning designs a root microbial community for alfalfa in saline-alkali soil
summary: From 327 salt-alkali-tolerant root bacterial strains, 20 complementary strains were assembled into 134 stochastic synthetic communities tested in germination assays. Random forest and elastic-net GLM models then selected five key strains for the community SP3. In pot experiments under salt-alkali stress SP3 increased alfalfa plant height by 62.0% and root length by 91.1% over single-strain and two-strain inoculations, and in a saline-alkali field it raised aboveground dry biomass by 48.1% over the untreated control. One crop and one field site.
ai_technology: Random forest and elastic-net GLM models of strain interactions from synthetic-community assays

evidence.tested: Pot experiments under salt-alkali stress and a field trial in saline-alkali soil.
evidence.unknown: Generality across crops, sites and years; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models selected the key strains for the final community.
